title: Database-Specific Injection
description: Database-specific primitives that can amplify an injection flaw.

attacks.name: Stacked queries
attacks.desc: Allowing multiple statements in one SQL input can turn one injection point into additional database operations.
attacks.prevention: Use parameterized queries and disable multi-statement execution where the driver supports it.

attacks.name: LOAD_FILE()
attacks.desc: MySQL's LOAD_FILE can read server-side files when permissions and injection context allow it.
attacks.prevention: Use a least-privilege database account without file-read permissions, and eliminate the injection path.

attacks.name: INTO OUTFILE
attacks.desc: MySQL's INTO OUTFILE can write query output to a server-side file when the account has sufficient privileges.
attacks.prevention: Remove file-write privileges from application accounts and keep query values bound as data.

attacks.name: xp_cmdshell
attacks.desc: SQL Server's xp_cmdshell can invoke operating-system commands if enabled and reachable through an injection path.
attacks.prevention: Disable xp_cmdshell unless indispensable, restrict privileged SQL roles, and parameterize application queries.

attacks.name: MSSQL stacked + EXEC
attacks.desc: Stacked SQL Server statements can call EXEC or other operations beyond the intended query.

attacks.name: Postgres COPY ... FROM PROGRAM
attacks.desc: PostgreSQL's COPY FROM PROGRAM can execute a server-side program when the database role has the required privileges.

attacks.name: Postgres large object read
attacks.desc: PostgreSQL large-object functions can expose server-side file content when privileged functions are reachable.

attacks.name: Oracle UTL_HTTP / UTL_FILE
attacks.desc: Oracle UTL_HTTP and UTL_FILE can reach network or file resources when grants and injection context permit it.

attacks.name: SQLite file read
attacks.desc: SQLite file-reading extensions or functions can expose local files if enabled in the application environment.

attacks.name: MySQL error-based (EXTRACTVALUE)
attacks.desc: MySQL error messages from XML-related functions can disclose query results in affected versions and configurations.

attacks.name: Time-based per-DB payloads
attacks.desc: Database-specific delay functions can reveal query truth through response timing when direct output is unavailable.

attacks.name: OOB DNS exfil
attacks.desc: A database feature that performs network lookups can leak data through DNS when reachable from an injection point.
